Re: Appeal of denial of prior authorization for partial knee replacement  
CPT 27446

Dear Grievances and Appeals Department:

I am appealing Blue Cross of Idaho’s denial dated August 18, 2026, of prior authorization for partial knee replacement, CPT 27446. The denial states that the imaging findings submitted did not support medical necessity.

The submitted clinical record supports the requested procedure and directly addresses the imaging concern:

- The July 12, 2026 MRI documents full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment, with bone-on-bone apposition.
- The MRI also documents Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medial disease.
- The symptoms have progressively worsened for 12 months and have not been relieved by rest.
- I completed 20 supervised physical-therapy visits focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion from June 1 through July 27, 2026, without adequate relief.
- NSAID treatment for four months was inadequate.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 30, 2026, provided only four weeks of partial relief.
- The condition substantially limits daily function: I cannot climb stairs without assistance and wake three to four times each night because of pain.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- The record documents no active infection, no untreated substance-use disorder, BMI 29, and no smoking history.
- The requested procedure was submitted by Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery.

The imaging does not merely show mild or nonspecific degenerative changes. It shows complete cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone contact and grade 4 medial disease. Those findings are consistent with the persistent pain, restricted motion, sleep disruption, and severe functional limitation documented in the clinical record.

Please conduct a complete reconsideration of the denial using the MRI report, physical-therapy discharge note, medication and injection history, examination findings, and the surgeon’s clinical assessment. Please reverse the denial and approve CPT 27446.

I also request that Blue Cross of Idaho provide the exact medical policy or InterQual criteria, including the version used for this determination, that were applied to reference number POC-BDA4258628-91913. I was unable to identify a publicly available Blue Cross of Idaho policy containing the medical-necessity criteria for CPT 27446. Accordingly, this appeal does not quote plan policy language; the argument above is based on the clinical records and the stated denial reason.

Please acknowledge receipt of this appeal and provide the determination in writing. If additional information is required, please contact me or my treating surgeon promptly.

Sincerely,

Reese Foster
